column1: Similarly, consider these two events: n Gates buys $5 million in IBM stock from Buffett on the New York Stock Exchange. n General Motors sells $10 million in stock to the public and uses the proceeds to build a new car factory. Here, investment is $10 million. The first transaction reallocates ownership of shares in IBM from Buffett to Gates; the economy’s stock of capital is unchanged, so there is no investment as macroeconomists use the term. By contrast, because General Motors is using some of the economy’s output of goods and services to add to its stock of capital, its new factory is counted as investment.
